subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & rate limits - next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & rate limits - next steps

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to hear how Acme is planning to add semantic search + reranking on top of your existing search stack. Quick recap and a set of concrete questions so we can scope an integration and prepare the SRE/solutions-engineer deep-dive: 

Recap
- Use case: user-facing semantic search (embeddings-based recall) + a lightweight reranker (ML model) to improve relevance on top results; some tool-calling/structured output for entity extraction in results.
- Platform: primarily cloud-hosted (K8s + API gateway), multi-region (mostly us-west), SOC2 in progress.
- Priority: low-latency for search (p95 < 250ms where possible), predictable cost for embeddings + reranker.

Questions (could you confirm?):
1) Expected traffic profile: what's your steady-state QPS for search vs. peak burst QPS? any predictable hourly/daily patterns?
2) Auth: do you prefer service-account API keys, or will you want OAuth/JWT-based short-lived tokens from your identity provider?
3) Routing / regions: do you need strict regional pinning (data residency) or is cross-region fallback OK?
4) Embeddings/re-ranker details: embedding dim, typical batch sizes, reranker candidate counts (top-K), and whether you'd like Redwood to host reranker or run as a sidecar.
5) Rate limits & retries: can you tolerate 429s for short periods with client retries? Do you have an existing idempotency key pattern for stateful calls (ingestion)?

Attachments: I referenced the architecture diagram you shared in the call — please attach if available (acme-llm-arch.pdf) and any SOC2 artifacts (acme-soc2-qa.xlsx) that we should review.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineer) & Rishi (platform architect) — 60 min to go over routing, auth, batching, and retry semantics.
- Redwood will prepare a short integration checklist and a recommended client-side retry/backoff pattern plus idempotency guidance.
- Procurement intro (if applicable) so we can get an NDA/PO in motion.

Proposed times (PDT): Wed 6/24 10–12 or Thu 6/25 9–11. Which works best?

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments referenced: acme-llm-arch.pdf (architecture diagram), acme-soc2-qa.xlsx (SOC2 Q&A)

From: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & rate limits - next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline below and attaching the architecture diagram we sketched during the call.

Answers:
- Traffic: steady-state search QPS ~50 (global), predictable spikes up to ~200 QPS for promotional bursts; average embedding requests are ~30 QPS but batched from our side.
- Auth: we use JWTs at the gateway for user requests, but for server-to-server we prefer service account API keys (we can provision keys per vendor).
- Routing: primary region is us-west-2; cross-region fallback is OK for non-PHI data.
- Embeddings/reranker: embeddings are 512-dim, we batch at 64–128 per request, reranker runs over top-20 candidates typically. We currently run the reranker in our ML infra but are open to Redwood-hosted options if it simplifies latency.
- Rate limits & retries: we can tolerate transient 429s for short windows if client retries with exponential backoff and jitter. For ingestion/persistent writes we can generate idempotency keys; search is read-only so idempotency is not required for queries.

Procurement contact: Mark Ellis (mark.ellis@acmecorp.com) — loop him in for commercial/PO discussions.

I attached: acme-llm-arch.pdf (architecture diagram). SOC2 spreadsheet will follow next week (we're finalizing answers).

Cheers,
Sophie
Head of Search Platform | Acme Corp

Attachment: acme-llm-arch.pdf (application topology diagram)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & rate limits - next steps

Sophie — great, that helps a lot. Looping in Marissa and Rishi to schedule the deep-dive and map technical owners. High-level recommendations based on your answers: 

- Auth: we can support service-account API keys (scoped, revocable) and JWT-based short-lived tokens via our token exchange if you want to integrate with your IDP.
- SDK / batching: use our client SDK to handle embedding batching (client-side batch sizes 32–128) and automatic parallelization for reranker candidates. SDKs also provide built-in request IDs and optional automatic deduplication for ingestion calls.
- Rate limiting & retries: follow this pattern:
  * Respect 429 + Retry-After header when provided.
  * Exponential backoff with full jitter (base 200ms, max 30s) for retries.
  * Use idempotency keys (Idempotency-Key or X-Request-ID) for any ingestion/stateful calls so retries are safe.
  * For read/search traffic, prefer client-side smoothing (token bucket) + local batching to reduce spiky QPS.
  * For streaming responses, include a request-id header that is echoed back by Redwood so you can reconcile partial streams.
- Routing: we recommend regional pinning (us-west primary) with automatic fallback to us-east if capacity constrained; Redwood will surface per-route quotas in the Console so you can set alerts.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (60m) — attendees: Sophie, Mark (procurement, optional), Marissa (solutions eng), Rishi (platform). Proposed slots: Wed 6/24 10:30–11:30 PDT or Thu 6/25 09:00–10:00 PDT. Please confirm.
2) We'll send a short integration checklist (attached: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf) and a sample client retry snippet showing exponential backoff + jitter and idempotency headers.
3) I'll open a HubSpot opportunity and attach the SOC2 artifacts once you send them.

Links: HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/ACME-42
DocuSign (sample terms): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abcd-1234

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
